note: The four sound slots of a reel. Every number here was measured by decoding the file at 48 kHz mono (python3 tools/sound.py probe <name>), never read off a filename. Slices are [start, end] in seconds of the source; target_rms_db is the level the slot is normalised to before it enters the mix. A film's audio/build_final.py names the file and copies the slice and target into its own knobs.

licences.pixabay: Pixabay Content License - free for commercial use, no attribution, may not be redistributed as a standalone audio file.
licences.mixkit: Mixkit Free License - free for commercial and non-commercial use inside a video, no attribution, may not be redistributed as a standalone audio file.
licences.generated: Made by this engine from the numbers in the slot, so there is nothing to clear and nothing to attribute. tools/sound.py renders it.
licences.unclearable: Source could not be established and the file carries no licence. Not 'probably fine' - unusable in a published film. Audition only.

provenance.note: What the files themselves prove about where this library came from. Read before adding a file: a filename is not a source, and this folder is a compilation, not one pack.

groups.files: the numbered cinematic set - 01 Boom, 02 Deep, 03/04 Grand Hit, 05 Impact, 06 Drum Roll, 07/08 Subsonic, 09 Struck Down, 10 Dark Drop, 11 Low Quick, 11/12 Universe Boom, 13 Metal Slam, plus 01 Beating ... 29 Swing A
groups.format: 96 kHz / 24-bit stereo PCM WAV with a Logic Pro X BWF header: JUNK chunk, time_reference, umid, and an empty originator and coding history
groups.dates: embedded date tags 2019-04-15 to 2019-05-07, in two vintages (04-15..20 and 05-06/07)
groups.verdict: Not a shipped library. A library delivers UCS-named files with Soundminer metadata and a filled originator; these are bare re-exports from somebody's Logic Pro X session over three weeks in 2019, with no originator, no pack name and no licence text in the folder. No public pack matches these filenames. The source is unidentifiable, which makes the licence unclearable rather than merely unknown.

start.role: the engine catching, alone, before the first word. 1.0-2.6 s
start.why: cranking, firing, settling, then an idle behind it. Quiet recording: normalise, never guess a multiplier.

alternates.why: it cranks and never catches, then dies away by 1.7 s. For the Why It Failed angle; nothing may follow it but silence.
a modern V8 barks and settles. 1980s and later cars; too clean for a flathead.

bed.role: the running engine under the whole film, ducked beneath every word. looped with a 0.30 s crossfade
bed.why: 6.0 s of the evenest idle in the library, -10 to -14 dB the whole way: a lumpy cam that loops without a seam.

alternates.why: the bed of the first three films. Flat and very quiet: it needs the 7.5 make-up gain those builds carry.
5.25 s of near-flat idle at -30 dB. For a luxury car: present, never busy.
for a truck, a van or anything with a clatter. Never for a V8.

roar.role: the closing 2.0 s, after the last word, with no voice over it
roar.why: one clean roar, front-loaded, gone by 2.2 s. 20 ms fade in, 300 ms fade out.

alternates.why: two revs inside the two seconds. For a car whose point is throttle response.
the closing roar of the Mustang and the SC/Rambler.
a real car pulling away instead of revving on the spot. It dies away inside the two seconds.

hit.role: one low hit under the closing card. The only hit in the film
hit.why: 58 Hz sliding to 40 Hz, gone in a quarter of a second: tighter than any recording in the folder, and ours by construction, so there is no licence to establish. The same thud the published SC/Rambler used, with a 2 ms attack so it cannot click.

alternates.why: front-loaded boom, -22 dB by half a second, 1.3 s long. Bigger and colder than the synth; the one recorded hit here whose licence is known.

DO NOT SHIP. The best-measuring thud in the folder, but it is one of the unnamed 96 kHz Logic Pro X re-exports in provenance group 1 - no originator, no pack, no licence. Kept only because it is worth hearing what to match.

rest: The other ~165 files are UI clicks, camera shutters, keyboard typing, clock ticks, paper, notifications, cartoon voices and generic swishes. None of them is a car, so none belongs in a reel. They stay in the folder because deleting the person's files is not the engine's call; the kit simply never points at them.
A future angle that needs one of them adds it to a slot here, with a measured slice and a licence - never straight into a build_final.py.

Anything from provenance group 1 (the unnamed 96 kHz Logic Pro X set) stays out of a build until its source is established somewhere better than a filename. An unclearable file is a liability on a page that posts publicly; a generated one costs nothing and can be tuned tighter.
